repeatability.selection: Every 18th of the 216 native condition groups in sorted order

illustration.rule: Cell (load, scenario, profile) with the most falls prevented in the contact model at 0.25 ms among cells that both gains survive under exact feedback in all three plants; then the lowest seed index at which the fixed gain falls and the payload-aware gain survives in both the planar and the 0.25 ms contact model.

hardware_plan.rule: Boundary-shift cells (H4), from the contact model at 0.25 ms, 0.3 N m, -7 deg: the load with the largest predicted shift, the load at 0.26 m with the largest shift, and the load with the smallest absolute shift (null). Staircase: one up, one down, step 2% of the predicted boundary, start one step below it, estimate = mean commanded push after the first six trials; realised push scatter assumed 3% (standard deviation) of the commanded push. Trials per gain and cell: smallest number for which a two one-sided test with a ±3% equivalence margin has 90% power at zero true shift (alpha 0.05 each side), from 4,000 simulated staircases. Contrast cells (H5): both gains survive with exact feedback in all three plants, not the delayed profile (in simulation it drives the torque into a sustained full-torque limit cycle that an ideal torque source can produce and a real motor driver may not), and a noisy net fall reduction of at least 10 of 30 seeds in the planar model and at both contact steps; at most one cell per load, largest contact-model reduction first. Pairs needed: exact two-sided sign test, alpha 0.05, power 0.9, assuming hardware prevents falls half as often as the contact simulation and introduces them 5 percentage points more often.
